---
title: MIR 1.0.0 F200 migration-origin successors
---

This fixture is a private successor observer for the protected MIR 1.0.0 F200 source save. It deliberately retains the source fixture mod identity and storage key so that configuration change loads the exact original state rather than manufacturing a replacement baseline.

The F200 wrapper is version `0.2.0` and admits only Base 2.0.77 with MIR `5.0.20000`. The F210 wrapper is version `0.3.0` and admits only Base 2.1.23 with MIR `5.0.21000`. Both begin directly from the same immutable MIR1 source save; no intervening MIR5 installation is part of either origin claim. Both wrappers are staged as `info.json` from the target-specific metadata file and have no alternate runtime members.

Before any candidate work, the control reads all retained source rows, state fields, recipe bonuses, effect signatures, foreign queue, detached work, manual-mining offset, and the effective false breeding setting. It does not seed or silently skip source research; the separate fixture-owned sentinel handling below is not evidence of arbitrary external modifier preservation. The wrapper supplies the source's observed false breeding startup input for this bounded successor load; it does not claim that the historical fixture default was a user-authored override that persists through a later default change. Source science and cost remain historical facts; the candidate gear lab uses the candidate's actual runtime science list after the observer data stage has reduced only that lab's count and time.

The source fixture itself seeded and snapshotted the player, foreign, and detached manual-mining offsets. Configuration first validates retained source rows, effects, recipe contributions, queues and direct gear without writing the source. Only then does it admit the observed zero or the saved0.125 value for all three fixture-owned fields; every other value, including finite0.25 drift, is refused before reapplication. It re-applies zero only, retains an already-correct value, and never writes the sentinel on a cold reload. This records fixture-owned baseline handling. The separately retained [early-entry diagnostic and original successor evidence](../../../../spec/evidence/migration-origin-100-direct-successor-native-chain.json) records zero before MIR callbacks in its exact native closure; it does not qualify this later corrected fixture or arbitrary unowned modifiers. A zero observed later in the lifecycle alone does not establish an engine-caused reset.

The original MIR1 effect snapshot stays raw in source storage. The successor comparison accepts only the independently observed F200/F210 representation differences for additive `change-recipe-productivity` records: omission of an explicit `hidden=false`, the four authored finite float32 values (`.10`, `.05`, `.02`, `.01`) represented at their original source precision, and record ordering. It preserves every record's multiplicity and rejects changed recipe, type, change, `hidden=true`, missing, or duplicate effects; it neither rounds arbitrary values nor rewrites the stored source signature.

One real candidate gear completion is required for each successor. It is recorded separately from the one historical source lab, then the completed save must survive two read-only cold reloads. This fixture makes no physical-factory, performance, or release claim.
